title: CMOS inverter amplifier
description: A CMOS inverter used as an analog amplifier: the input drives both an NMOS and a PMOS gate, and the two devices share one drain current stacked between the rails (current reuse). Because both transconductances act on the same input, the stage transconductance is the sum $g_{m,tot} = g_{m,n} + g_{m,p}$, so the inverter gives roughly twice the $g_m$ of a single device at the same current - the reason it is the workhorse gain cell for low-voltage, power-efficient design. The gain is $g_{m,tot}/(g_{ds,n} + g_{ds,p})$. Both devices are composed children biased at the same current; pick the PMOS child table to the p polarity and set p_sign to -1 for a signed-PMOS axis.

params.name: V_out
params.note: output DC level; sets both devices' drain-source voltages (ideally near mid-supply)

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate (both drains + wiring); refine from extraction

params.name: I_bias
params.note: the single current both devices carry (current reuse)

params.name: gm_id_p
params.note: PMOS inversion. Matching it to gm_id_n balances the transfer and minimizes offset, but the two devices share one gate, so the choice is also what places the input level — see the V_in row: at these defaults the two binds ask that node for different voltages

params.name: p_sign
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS table: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: NMOS device
doc.description: The pull-down device at the shared current, drain at the output. Exposes its transconductance, output conductance, saturation headroom, current, and channel-noise density. Its wiring declaration is TAUTOLOGICAL as the sheet stands: the input level $V_{in}$ is derived from this device’s own gate-source voltage, so the declared node and the checked node are the same number and the check cannot fire. It is kept because it stops being tautological the moment someone re-types $V_{in}$ as a plain parameter — which is exactly the defect this mechanism was built after.

doc.title: PMOS device
doc.description: The pull-up device at the shared current, drain at the output. Exposes its transconductance, output conductance, saturation headroom, and current.

params.name: vds_d
params.note: source-to-drain headroom, signed to this table's axis convention

rows.name: V_in
rows.note: the input DC level, read off the NMOS bind: its source is at ground, so the gate sits at its own gate-source voltage. The PMOS shares that gate, and the wiring declarations on both children check the two devices against this one node — at the shipped defaults they DISAGREE, which is the sheet's known open problem: gm_id_n and gm_id_p are offered as two free knobs when one shared gate leaves only one of them free. Set the two inversion levels so both devices land on the same input level, or size against a supply that can carry both

rows.name: gm_tot
rows.note: current reuse: both devices' transconductances act on the same input and add

rows.name: gout
rows.note: both output conductances load the node

rows.name: Av
rows.note: combined transconductance into the combined output conductance

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: both channel-noise currents (each device's own vnth_m*gm) sum and refer to the input by gm_tot

rules.note: NMOS saturated at the output DC level
PMOS saturated: its headroom is the supply minus the output level
combined gm over the total output capacitance
